question: How can natural language processing and machine learning techniques be leveraged to improve the understanding of medical jargon and research papers for non-experts?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer frames high-Q dielectric optical microcavities (microspheres, microtoroids, bottles, microdisks) supporting whispering-gallery modes via total internal reflection at the circumference as the basis for ultra-precise biosensing.
examples: Light circulates via total internal reflection, forming a WGM resonance with a standing-wave electric field profile
Microspheres, microtoroids, bottles, and microdisks serve as resonant biosensing platforms with extreme precision

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes how the WGM resonance is excited and probed, e.g., via tapered fibre or prism coupling, with typical Q-factors of 10^(6-7).
examples: The resonance is probed with a tapered fibre or prism
Q-factors of one million to ten million are common

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains the reactive sensing principle: adsorbed biomolecules perturb the evanescent field and change the local refractive index, red-shifting (detuning) the resonance frequency.
examples: Adsorption increases the effective refractive index and shifts the mode to the red
The reactive sensing principle links mass adsorption to frequency shift

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that a nanoparticle lifts the degeneracy between clockwise and counter-clockwise WGMs, splitting the resonance into a doublet whose separation encodes particle properties such as polarizability.
examples: A nanoparticle breaks CW/CCW degeneracy, producing a doublet in the transmission spectrum
Splitting magnitude relates to particle polarizability, enabling sizing

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains that particle-induced scattering or absorption losses broaden the WGM resonance linewidth as a third detection route.
examples: NP scattering or absorption broadens the resonance linewidth
Linewidth broadening can be used to infer particle size

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer conveys key perturbation-theory results: the shift is proportional to surface density and excess polarizability, inversely proportional to cavity radius (1/R), highly sensitive to adsorption location with 1/R^(5/2) scaling in the most sensitive region, and validated by measurements (e.g., BSA surface areas matching crystallographic data).
examples: Shift ∝ surface density × excess polarizability / R
The most sensitive adsorption region gives shifts varying as 1/R^(5/2); estimated BSA surface areas match crystallographic data

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer cites demonstrated label-free capabilities: detection of 2.5 nm nanoparticles and 15.5 kDa molecules in aqueous solution using laser-frequency locking to improve signal-to-noise, and sizing of individual dielectric nanoparticles and virus particles.
examples: Laser-frequency locking enabled detection of 2.5 nm nanoparticles and 15.5 kDa molecules
Single dielectric NPs and virus particles have been sized

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer mentions practical implementation details, including tapered-fibre/prism coupling with Q-factors of 10^(6-7) and novel cavity geometries such as pressure-compensated hollow-bottle microresonators fabricated by a soften-and-compress method, tolerant to angular misalignment and exhibiting spectral clean-up.
examples: Soften-and-compress fabrication yields hollow-bottle resonators tolerant to misalignment
Hollow-bottle resonators show spectral clean-up from localized losses

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer acknowledges that, despite these capabilities, direct detection of single-molecule binding on a pristine WGM cavity has not yet been achieved.
examples: Single-molecule binding detection on a pristine WGM cavity remains an outstanding challenge
No direct single-molecule binding detection on bare WGM cavities to date
